requirements.statement: The page's 'Back' link goes to the Commodity details page (consignment details) in the linear journey; when the page was opened from the hub, review or template review, the journey's own back-link rule applies.
requirements.why: DR2.1 places identification straight after commodity details, so Back returns there; the prototype wins by default.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the back link always returns to the notification Overview (repo-frontend-p6-005, trace-animals-fit-p10-012).

requirements.statement: The page is a journey step when at least one selected species has identifier fields. Commodity details then continues to it; otherwise the journey skips it, and a direct GET or POST to it redirects to the next step after Commodity details.
requirements.why: DR2.1 puts identification in the linear flow after commodity details and skips it when there is nothing to identify. With the free-text fallback V4 asks for (req-animal-identification-008, req-animal-identification-009), every selected species has identifier fields, so in practice the page is a step for every consignment and the skip never fires.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the page is reached only from the Overview's task row, and a direct visit with nothing to identify redirects to the Overview (trace-e2e-p6-004, repo-frontend-p6-009), not to the next journey step.

requirements.statement: In the live-animals set, 'Save and continue' on a valid identification page reached through the journey goes to the next journey page: Additional details where that page applies, otherwise Arrival details. When the page was opened from its overview task, the review or template review, it returns there instead.
requirements.why: DR2.1 runs the journey page to page. The 9 October ruling splits this requirement into a live half (this one) and a germinal half, and confirms that a page opened from its overview task returns to the overview on Save and continue, with no new from-hub marker.
requirements.deltaNote: Today Save and continue always redirects to the Overview (trace-animals-fit-p10-079, trace-e2e-p6-057), even when the trader came through the journey from Commodity details.

requirements.statement: The page ends with the shared journey actions: 'Save and continue', 'Save and return to overview' (saves, then returns to the overview) and the link 'Cancel and return to overview', with the amend and template-review variants the journey uses elsewhere.
requirements.why: Both versions end the page on the same three controls.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p10-077 shows the same button group today; the amend and template variants belong to the journey-flow and templates areas.

requirements.statement: In the live-animals set, 'Save and continue' and 'Save and return to overview' save the typed identifiers of every species panel whose form holds a value, including a species with more than one animal.
requirements.why: The 26 October ruling's principle that what a trader typed is never dropped, which is also what the service does today; DR2.1 instead drops a multi-animal species' typed values unless its own panel button was pressed, which its own source notes as a silent loss. Whether the principle reaches the page's save buttons is the open question the default settles for now. The 9 October ruling splits this requirement; the germinal half is req-250.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-072 and trace-animals-fit-p10-080 show a save recording one new animal for every panel whose form holds data today.

requirements.statement: A species panel's own save button checks every open species panel and saves one animal for each panel whose form holds a value, then reloads the page showing the next animal to enter.
requirements.why: The 26 October ruling's principle that what a trader typed is never dropped, which is what the service does today; DR2.1 instead checks and saves only the panel whose button was pressed. Whether the principle reaches a panel save is the open question the default settles for now.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-072 and p6-073 show a panel save checking every open card and appending a record for each card holding data today, and repo-frontend-p6-071 the reload.

requirements.statement: Pressing Enter in a field never presses a species panel's Remove button or another panel's save button: the field's default submit is a submit button that is visually hidden, aria-hidden and not focusable.
requirements.why: A real-service safeguard DR2.1 does not show: without it Enter would press the first panel or Remove button. The 26 October ruling then decides what that default submit does (req-animal-identification-017, req-animal-identification-018), so the safeguard holds per panel rather than once for the whole form.
requirements.deltaNote: Today one hidden 'finish' submit button at the top of the form serves every field on the page (repo-frontend-p6-076, trace-e2e-p6-060), whichever panel the field belongs to.

requirements.statement: The page keeps the real service's mechanics: its address under the notification (commodities/identification), its entry guard, a CSRF crumb and concurrency token on every post, server-side validation only, values that fail validation never saved, and errors shown only on the response to the failing submission.
requirements.why: Persistence, authentication and validation are real constraints the prototype cannot express, and the ruling lets them override it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-073 and trace-animals-fit-p11-001 show today's server-side re-render without saving; repo-frontend-p6-077 the crumb and token; repo-perftests-p1-025 shows the k6 suite already driving the page at commodities/identification.

requirements.statement: The 'Selected commodities' summary has one row per selected commodity with the columns 'Commodity code', 'Common name', 'Species' and the quantity column; a commodity with several species lists each species on its own line in the Species cell, and the quantity cell shows the row's number of animals.

The 9 October afternoon ruling holds inc-051 with the commodity catalogue: none of these commodities is in today's five-commodity live catalogue, and the catalogue waits on MDM.
requirements.blockedBy: Commodities come from MDM: pigs, sheep and goats join the live-animals catalogue only through the MDM commodity integration, which this programme cannot build (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm, claims 28, 29 and 32: inc-051 waits with the catalogue).

requirements.why: Where a real rule is kept, DR2.1's wording for the same kind of rule is used; it also matches the address-length errors' 'or less'.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the messages say 'characters or fewer' (repo-frontend-p6-021 to p6-025).

requirements.statement: Identifier values are trimmed of surrounding spaces before they are checked and saved, so surrounding spaces never count towards the length limit.
requirements.why: DR2.1 trims before checking; today trims only what it saves.

requirements.statement: Each identifier error appears in an error summary titled 'There is a problem', in field order, linking to and focusing its own field (field ids unique per commodity line and field, in the real service's naming), and inline on the field in error.
requirements.why: Both versions link each error to the field it is about. Field names and ids are architecture, which the prototype never decides (c-039), so today's per-line ids stay; with one line per species they are already unique per species.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p11-004 and p11-005 show summary links that focus the field and inline errors today, with per-line field ids (repo-frontend-p6-018).

requirements.statement: When a save fails validation, the page is shown again with the values the user typed kept in the form.
requirements.why: Both versions keep what the trader typed.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-e2e-p6-043 shows typed values kept after a failed add today.

requirements.statement: In the live-animals set, an animal counts as entered once at least one identifier its species asks for has a value: it is saved, listed in the saved-animals table and the panel moves on to the next animal, with the other identifiers left blank.
requirements.why: Sam's 9 October ruling: one identifier is enough, for the Complete status and for submit, and DR1 inc-103 (every identifier filled) is closed and not built. V4 says the same from the other side: every animal identifier field is optional on its own, and the block is satisfied by at least one of them. It holds 'for now' on the footing that it is no change, which today's service confirms.
requirements.deltaNote: Today one identifier is enough: a cow with only an ear tag and a dog with only a microchip are saved and listed (trace-e2e-p6-102, trace-animals-fit-p10-065, repo-frontend-p6-019).

requirements.statement: In the live-animals set, pressing a species panel's 'Save and add another' or 'Save and finish' with every identifier of the current animal blank saves nothing and shows 'Enter at least one identifier for this animal' in the error summary and inline, linked to that panel's first identifier field. The check is made per panel, so an empty panel is refused even when another species' form holds data. A partly filled animal saves with no error. The page's 'Save and continue' and 'Save and return to overview' never block on missing identifiers: an empty form saves no record and the trader moves on, and the page shows no message about the submit rule.
requirements.why: One identifier is enough (9 October ruling), so DR1's per-identifier errors, which it asked for only if every identifier were ruled required, are not built. An animal with no identifier at all is not a record, and validation is a real constraint the prototype cannot express, so today's at-least-one error stays where DR2.1 silently keeps the trader on the same animal (c-042).
requirements.deltaNote: Today the message, its link and the partial save exist (repo-frontend-p6-027, trace-animals-fit-p11-006), but the empty check fires only when no card anywhere on the page holds data, so an empty card beside a filled one is skipped silently (document-dr1-parity-backlog-p5-019).

requirements.statement: The saved-animals table lists every saved animal, including one saved with only some of its identifiers; an identifier left blank shows as an empty cell.
requirements.why: A record with one identifier counts as identified (9 October ruling), so it is listed like any other; DR2.1's complete-only listing rested on its every-identifier rule, which the ruling sets aside (c-041).
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p10-063 and trace-e2e-p6-048 show every saved record listed today, with empty cells for identifiers left blank.

requirements.statement: The saved-animals table sits below the entry form and the panel save button, and shows both while animals are still being entered and once all are entered.
requirements.why: DR2.1's order puts the next animal's form first.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the table sits above the entry form (repo-frontend-p6-084, trace-animals-fit-p10-058).

requirements.statement: The saved-animals table has an 'Animal' column, one column per identifier the species asks for (headed with the field label), and a Remove action; each row is labelled '<species> <n>', such as 'Bos taurus 1'.

requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p10-060 and p10-061 show the Animal column, identifier columns and '<species> <n>' rows today.

requirements.statement: Each saved row has a 'Remove' button (visually hidden suffix 'animal <n>') that posts the form, deletes that animal straight away with no confirmation, renumbers later animals, reopens the entry form for the freed place, and deletes the species' identification record when its last animal is removed.

requirements.statement: In the live-animals set, the hub's Identification details row shows Complete on exactly the bar the notification must meet to submit (req-249), counting a saved animal with at least one identifier as identified: with one species selected it is Complete straight away; with several, it is Complete once each species with identifier fields has at least one such animal. That sets aside DR2.1's every-animal-complete rule (c-041) and matches what the service does today. requirements.statement: In the live-animals set, to submit: identification details are optional when only one species is selected; when more than one species is selected, each species with identifier fields needs at least one saved animal with at least one identifier. The ruling leaves the wording of the several-lines rule to the Behaviour Spec; the review-and-submit area owns the gate and its message. V4 asks instead for an identifier for each animal, which the ruling does not settle, so the gate rests on the open question c-animal-identification-004. The 9 October ruling splits this requirement; the germinal half is req-261.

conflicts.about: Whether the page takes the prototype's mount mechanics (its own URL, no entry guards, errors held in the session, invalid values saved).

positions.says: A real constraint the prototype cannot express, such as persistence, validation or authentication, overrides the prototype.
The page is served at /animal-identification-details under /design-release-2.1.
The page has no entry guards and can be opened at any point.
Errors are held in the session and shown again on reload.
Values that fail validation are written to the session before errors are shown.
Each identifier field is named identifiers[<species id>][<field id>] with the id identifier-<species id>-<field id>.
The prototype never decides architecture: URL paths, query parameter and form field names, data-model shape or code structure.
If any card has an error nothing is saved and the page re-renders with the values kept.

conflicts.outcome: Both rulings rank first. The 7 October ruling names persistence, validation and authentication as constraints that override the prototype, and the 9 October ruling keeps this conflict for that reason and adds that the prototype never decides URL paths or form field names. The page keeps the real address under its notification, its guard, CSRF and concurrency token and its own field names and ids, and never saves invalid values or replays errors from the session.

conflicts.about: Whether the real identifier validation and stale-action safeguards stay where DR2.1 has none.

positions.says: Validation and persistence are real constraints that override the prototype.
A live-animal identifier with no length limit is never rejected for its content.
A panel save for a species with no animal left to enter does nothing and returns to the page.
A remove request for a position that does not exist is ignored.
Each identifier value can be at most 58 characters.
An add for a card already at its cap saves nothing and shows the cap-reached error.
A remove naming a record that does not exist is refused with 400.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling ranks first: the 58-character identifier limit, the cap-reached error for a stale add and the 400 for a bad remove stay. Where DR2.1 words the same kind of rule, its wording is used: '<label> must be 58 characters or less'. prototype-dr2-1-source-p5-066 is not overruled: its other half (removing the last animal deletes the species' record) still stands.

conflicts.about: When an animal (or a germinal entry) counts as identified, and what bar the Complete status sets: one identifier filled, or every identifier its species asks for and every animal entered.

positions.says: One identifier is enough: a record with one identifier counts as identified, for the Complete status and for submit.
There is no separate, stricter bar for the Complete status than for submit.
DR1 inc-103 (counting an animal as identified only once every identifier is filled in) is closed and not built.
The prototype wins by default; only a DR1 judgement on the same difference or a real constraint overrides it.
An animal's entry counts as complete only when every identifier field for its species has a value.
The saved-animals table shows only complete entries; a partly filled entry is not listed.
Identification is complete only when every animal of every species with fields is saved and complete; a germinal species only needs its one entry to exist.
A cattle animal is saved only when both Ear tag and Passport are filled in.
No single identifier is mandatory; one identifier is enough to save an animal.
Design release 1 holds a trader on an animal until every identifier for that commodity has a value.
Whether DR1's every-identifier rule or V4's at-least-one rule governs inc-103 is undecided; only the design authority can say.
inc-103 is deferred, held for a separate adjudication pass.
inc-103 is open and unruled, held for the design authority.
The frontend counts an animal as identified once one identifier is filled, matching V4's 'At least one Animal Identifier'.
Design release 1 counts an animal as entered only when every identifier has a value and lists only complete animals.

conflicts.outcome: The 9 October ruling ranks first and answers this difference directly, withdrawing the earlier reading under which the 7 October ruling's prototype default made every identifier required. One identifier is enough: a live animal saved with at least one identifier is entered, listed in the saved table and moved past; the Complete status uses exactly the submit bar (optional with one species, at least one identified record per species with several), with no stricter every-animal bar; DR1 inc-103 is closed and not built. The same one-record bar applies to the germinal set's entries: a germinal entry counts once it holds at least one value, not merely because it was saved. This is what the service does today. repo-frontend-p6-019 and document-dr1-parity-backlog-p5-016 back the winning rule and are not overruled; ruling-sam-2026-10-07-p1-008 still stands as the general look-and-feel default and is not overruled. For the germinal set a lone species is not exempt: V4 asks for at least one germinal identifier per animal, so every selected germinal species, one or several, needs an entry holding at least one value (c-277). V4 agrees from the other side: every one of its six animal identifier fields is marked optional on its own while the field block is satisfied by at least one of them (confluence-6497338582-p4-003, p4-005), so one identifier is enough for a record. How many animals and species must hold such a record before submit is no longer settled here: V4 asks for an identifier for each animal, which the ruling expressly does not cover, and that question is c-animal-identification-004.

conflicts.about: What a trader is told when they press a species panel's save with some or all of the animal's identifiers blank.

positions.says: One identifier is enough: a record with one identifier counts as identified.
Validation is a real constraint that overrides the prototype.
If every identifier is required, each empty box should name itself in the error summary, with new error copy, which DR1 does not supply.
A partly filled panel save keeps the same animal open with the values filled in and shows no error.
Save and finish with Passport blank and Ear tag filled does not save the animal and shows no error.
Save and finish with the passport blank does not save the animal, keeps the same panel open and shows no error.
An add with nothing entered shows 'Enter at least one identifier for this animal'; a partly filled animal saves.

conflicts.outcome: The 9 October ruling ranks first: one identifier is enough, so a partly filled animal saves with no error and the panel moves on, setting aside DR2.1's hold on the same animal. DR1's per-identifier errors were asked for only if every identifier were ruled required, which the ruling closes (c-041), so they are not built and the earlier outcome that adopted them is withdrawn. An animal with no identifier at all is not a record: validation is a real constraint the prototype cannot express (7 October ruling), so today's 'Enter at least one identifier for this animal', linked to the panel's first identifier field, stays where DR2.1 silently keeps the trader on the same animal; it is checked per panel. Save and continue and Save and return never block on missing identifiers, as in DR2.1. repo-frontend-p6-027 backs what is kept and is not overruled.

conflicts.about: What happens when a species' number of animals drops below its saved identification records.

positions.says: Keep the frontend's rule refusing a count lower than the records already entered, with its message (inc-094, Sam 2026-08-21).
Lowering the number of animals keeps the saved entries, and the table can list more animals than the new number.

conflicts.outcome: DR1 judged this same difference and ranks above the prototype. Commodity details refuses a count below the saved records with today's message and links to the species' panel; the over-count message stays as the safety net.

conflicts.about: Whether the per-animal permanent address leaves the identification page while DR1's address-space block stands.

positions.says: The prototype wins by default over what the real services do today.
Only a DR1 judgement on the same difference or a real constraint overrides the prototype.
Twelve address increments are blocked as deferred until the team's address work settles, and none may be built without a fresh ruling.
inc-057, which moves the whole permanent-address step into the consignment parties section, is blocked.
Some commodities ask for each animal's permanent address on the identification page.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling outranks the DR1 notes and is the fresh ruling the block waited for. The block was a hold against colliding work, not a judgement on the difference, so DR2.1 is built: the permanent address leaves this page for the permanent address page in consignment parties. DR1's buildable address increments on this page (inc-009, inc-059, inc-066) fall away with it. repo-frontend-p6-029 is not overruled: it describes today's page, which req-263 changes.

conflicts.about: Whether a species whose commodity requires no specific identifier type is asked for free-text identifiers, or asked nothing at all.

positions.says: The identification details field is shown when the given commodity has no specific identifier type, and captures free-text identification details.
The animal description field is shown on the same condition and captures a free-text animal description.
Where the commodity has no specific identifier type the two free-text fields stand in for one, so every commodity has some way of identifying its animals.
The page does not list which commodities have no specific identifier type, so the set can only be read as everything absent from the passport, tattoo, ear tag and horse name lists.
A species' identifier fields come from its commodity's entry in the identifiers list, and where there is no entry there are none.
For poultry there is no identification page at all: commodity details goes straight to additional details.
There is no free-text identifier fallback: a commodity with no declared identifiers is asked for none.
No field labelled 'Identification details' or 'Animal description' appears for any commodity walked.

conflicts.outcome: V4 ranks above the prototype, its traces and the real frontend, and sources.json makes it the specification of which data a notification captures, outranking the prototype on data even where a prototype claim says otherwise. The two free-text identifiers are built (req-animal-identification-008, req-animal-identification-009, req-animal-identification-010), so every selected species has a panel (req-210, req-221). Which commodities fall back is read as everything absent from V4's four identifier lists (confluence-6497338582-p4-061); in today's live catalogue that is Atlantic salmon alone, and poultry and the rest join with the MDM commodity catalogue. prototype-dr2-1-source-p5-013 is not overruled: its first half, that a species' identifier fields come from its commodity's own list, still stands and backs req-animal-identification-005, and only its 'otherwise there are none' half is set aside. prototype-dr2-1-specs-p4-017 keeps backing the half that still stands, that a species which needs identifying continues to the page. repo-frontend-p6-008 and trace-e2e-p6-017 describe today's page, which req-221 changes.

conflicts.about: Whether a tattoo identifier is asked for on cattle (0102) and pigs (0103), as V4's tattoo commodity list says, or only on cats, dogs and ferrets, as its list title's count of two, DR2.1 and today's service suggest.

positions.says: The commodities that require a tattoo identifier are 01061900 cats, dogs and ferrets, 0103 pigs and 0102 bovine.
The tattoo list's title says two commodities while five entries are listed, and the page does not say which figure is right.
The page names code 0102 'Cattle' in the passport and ear tag lists but 'Bovine' in the tattoo list.
Commodity code 0102 asks for two identifiers only, ear tag and passport.
Commodity code 0103 asks for one identifier, an ear tag.
A tattoo asked for on every cow is a defect of the real frontend's tattoo allowlist, and inc-110 corrects the commodity identifier sets.
A cow line shows ear tag and passport but no tattoo or microchip.

conflicts.outcome: V4 outranks the prototype and the DR1 notes on which commodities a rule covers, so the default follows its list and asks for a tattoo on cattle and pigs (req-animal-identification-013, req-animal-identification-014). It is a question rather than settled by precedence because V4 contradicts itself here: the list holds five entries while its title counts two, and it names the same code 'Bovine' in this list and 'Cattle' in the others, so the page does not say whether the list or the count is right. DR1's inc-110 is a todo finding, not a judgement on the difference, so it does not override.
conflicts.question: Does V4 mean a tattoo to be asked for on cattle (0102) and pigs (0103), which neither Design Release 2.1 nor the live service asks for today, or is its tattoo commodity list wider than intended, as its title's count of two suggests?
conflicts.default: Follow V4's list: a cattle panel asks for a tattoo after the ear tag and passport, and a pig panel asks for one as well as an ear tag when pigs reach the catalogue.

conflicts.about: Whether the notification still captures a microchip identifier, which V4's six animal identifier fields leave out.

positions.says: Six animal identifier fields are specified, at least one of which must be given, and none of them is a microchip.
The six animal identifier fields apply to the live animals journey only.
The page de-scopes an identifier type explicitly when it means to: the wing ring was de-scoped on 29 May 2026.
Commodity code 01061900 asks for a microchip, a passport and a tattoo.
Commodity code 0101 asks for a microchip, a passport and a horse name.
The identifier types the page can ask for are microchip, passport, tattoo, ear tag and horse name.

conflicts.outcome: The default keeps the microchip field, on cat, dog, ferret and horse panels, as DR2.1 shows it and the service asks for it today (req-animal-identification-012, req-222, req-223). V4 outranks the prototype on which data a notification captures, but it never says the microchip is out of scope, and it de-scopes a field explicitly when it means to, as it did for the wing ring; silence will not carry a user-visible field away.
conflicts.question: Does a notification still capture a microchip identifier, given that V4's animal identifier table specifies six fields and the microchip is not one of them, while the page de-scopes only the wing ring explicitly?
conflicts.default: The microchip field stays exactly as it is today and as Design Release 2.1 shows it, first on a cat, dog, ferret or horse panel.

conflicts.about: How much identification a live-animals notification must hold before it can be submitted: an identifier for every animal, or one identified animal per species and nothing at all when one species is selected.

positions.says: A notification cannot be submitted unless at least one animal identifier is given for each animal.
Design release 1's submit gate needs only one complete animal per species, and only when more than one species is selected.
Identification details are optional when only one species is selected; with several, each species with identifier fields needs at least one entry.
Sam's acceptance of one identifier being enough holds 'for now' and assumes it is a no-change, and the ruling does not say what happens if it turns out to need a change.
The ruling does not state how many identification records a notification with several lines needs.

conflicts.outcome: The default keeps the ruling: the 9 October ruling outranks V4 and accepted today's gate on the footing that it was no change, so identification stays optional with one species and needs one identified animal per species with several (req-248, req-249). V4's per-animal rule is recorded because the ruling expressly does not say how many records a notification needs, and because the germinal twin of this question went V4's way (c-277), which leaves the two sets on different bars until somebody settles this.
conflicts.question: Must every animal of every selected species carry at least one identifier before a live-animals notification can be submitted, as the V4 data-fields page says, or does today's gate stand, with identification optional for a single species?
conflicts.default: Today's gate stands: identification is optional when one species is selected, and with several each species with identifier fields needs at least one saved animal holding at least one identifier; the hub's Identification details row shows Complete on that same bar.

conflicts.about: Whether the 26 October ruling's principle that what a trader typed is never dropped reaches the identification page's own save buttons and a panel save, or only the Enter key on a panel for several animals.

positions.says: What a trader typed is never dropped, stated as a general principle and not limited to the identification page.
The recommendations Sam accepted are not quoted in the ruling, so how far the principle was meant to reach cannot be checked against his own words.
Save and continue saves the typed details only for single-animal species; what was typed into a multi-animal species' form is not saved unless its panel button was used.
A panel save validates and saves only that species' fields.
Any save on the page saves one new animal record for every panel whose form holds data, not only the panel whose button was pressed.

conflicts.outcome: The default keeps what the trader typed: every save on the page, whichever button, checks every open species panel and saves one animal for each panel holding a value, which is what the service does today (req-203, req-204). The 26 October ruling ranks above the prototype and states the principle in general terms, and the prototype's own source records its rule as a silent loss of a filled-in form; but the ruling's words reach only the Enter key, and the recommendation behind the principle is not quoted, so the two readings are left to the owner.
conflicts.question: Does 'what a trader typed is never dropped' apply to the identification page's 'Save and continue', 'Save and return to overview' and panel save buttons, so each of them saves every panel holding a value, or only to pressing Enter in a panel for several animals?
conflicts.default: Every save on the page checks every open species panel and saves one animal for each panel whose form holds a value, as the service does today; Design Release 2.1's rule of saving only the panel whose button was pressed is not built.

conflicts.about: What pressing Enter does in a field of a species panel for a single animal, or in a field outside any species panel.

positions.says: Pressing Enter in a field of a panel for several animals saves that panel, as its own save button does.
The ruling says nothing about pressing Enter in a single-animal panel or in a field outside a panel, so those cases are left open.
What a trader typed is never dropped, which would have Enter save wherever it is pressed.
Pressing Enter in a field submits the page as its default finish action, not as a panel save.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling settles the panel for several animals, which is adopted (req-animal-identification-017). For the rest of the page the default keeps today's behaviour: Enter in a single-animal panel and in a field outside any panel submits the page as 'Save and continue' (req-animal-identification-018), which saves that panel's animal anyway because a single-animal panel has no save button of its own.
conflicts.question: In a species panel for a single animal, and in a field outside any panel, should pressing Enter submit the page as 'Save and continue', as it does today, or save the panel the field belongs to?
conflicts.default: Enter in a single-animal panel, and in any field outside a panel, submits the page as 'Save and continue'; only a panel for several animals saves through its own panel save.
